thread.title: Three-team race in NFC North? Packers have bleak outlook after TNF disaster - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Three-team race in NFC North? Packers have bleak outlook after TNF disaster - NewsBreak

author: Will Ragatz
title: Three-team race in NFC North? Packers have bleak outlook after TNF disaster - NewsBreak
text:
By Will Ragatz ,
1 days ago
In what was a bit of a stunning sight, the Green Bay Packers were flat-out embarrassed by the Atlanta Falcons in a 35-14 loss at Lambeau Field on Thursday night. It’s too early to completely write off the Packers this season, but they have major issues that are going to be difficult to fix. So unless something changes quickly, the NFC North might be a three-team race in 2026.
After narrowly escaping with an overtime win over the Jets last week, the Packers were looking to get to 2-1 on the season in their home opener against a Falcons team that started 0-2 and lost by 31 to the Panthers last Sunday. Green Bay came into Thursday’s primetime contest having won 13 consecutive home openers.
Things started off well enough for the Packers, who intercepted Michael Penix Jr.’s third pass in his return to action. Green Bay took a 7-0 lead on a Jordan Love touchdown pass to Christian Watson. And then it all fell apart. The Falcons scored the next 27 points, nearly matching the 29 unanswered points the Vikings put on GB in Week 1.
Bijan Robinson ran for 194 yards and two touchdowns. Drake London caught nine passes for 194 yards of his own. The Falcons racked up 498 yards of offense, including 242 on the ground. Penix completed 16 of his 18 passes after a slow start in the first quarter. The Packers’ Micah Parsons-less defense did not record a single sack and offered basically no resistance after Atlanta’s first two possessions.
Somehow, the Packers’ issues on the offensive side of the ball are even more concerning. Green Bay ran for a grand total of 17 yards on eight carries in this game. They became completely one-dimensional, with Jordan Love attempting 53 passes. He completed just 28 of those (53 percent), and while he did throw for 312 yards and 2 TDs, a good chunk of that came in what was essentially garbage time.
The Packers’ offensive line is the biggest reason to think they may be in for a long season. With right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele out for the year and left guard Aaron Banks sidelined, the Packers rolled out an offensive line of Jordan Morgan, Jager Burton, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Anthony Belton. It was, somewhat predictably, a disaster.
Love was pressured on 25 dropbacks despite the Falcons barely blitzing. Burton, a fifth-round rookie, was charged with allowing 10 pressures. His PFF pass-blocking grade was 9.1 (out of 100). Another former fifth-round pick, Monk, was charged with six pressures. Belton and Morgan were each charged with five. Morgan and Rhyan were the only linemen who didn’t receive abysmal PFF marks. When pressured, Love was 9 of 23 with an interception and a sack.
Packers fans are in full-blown panic mode after this performance, and it’s not too difficult to see why. They can’t run the ball and are still at least a few weeks away from getting Josh Jacobs back. Their offensive line is a nightmare, which is generally pretty hard to overcome in the NFL. Love and the receivers can only do so much. The defense has real issues that Parsons can’t singlehandedly fix. They even had a field goal get blocked.
Here’s the Packers’ remaining schedule:
at Buccaneers vs. Bears vs. Cowboys at Lions vs. Panthers at Patriots vs. Vikings at Rams at Saints vs. Bills vs. Dolphins at Bears vs. Texans vs. Lions Miami is the only cakewalk in that mix. The Bucs, Cowboys, Panthers, and Saints seem to be varying degrees of solid. The Bears, Lions, Vikings, Patriots, Rams, Bills, and Texans are all probably good teams this year.
The outlook for the Packers does not look good right now. They were booed off the field on Thursday. Matt LaFleur didn’t have many answers in his postgame comments.
Maybe Green Bay will figure it out and bounce back. But the offensive line looks like a potential season-killer for the Packers. If that proves to be the case, the Vikings might only have two rivals to contend with in the NFC North this year.
